plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, PLTU, MUU) to zero.
Sell MSFU to reduce high-beta tech exposure.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration.
Hold remaining broad index ETFs (SPY, QQQ).
This plan prioritizes capital preservation.
Expect lower volatility and modest returns.
conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with lower volatility. Target monthly return is around 1.5%. Significant cash buffer and reduced leverage minimize drawdown risk.

moves.note: Add inverse ETF for risk hedge

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, PLTU, MUU) to low single digits.
Trim MSFU to reduce high-beta tech exposure.
Buy SOXS as a hedge against tech weakness.
Maintain significant exposure to broad index ETFs (SPY, QQQ).
This plan balances risk reduction with growth potential.
Target monthly return is around 2.5% with controlled risk.
balanced.read: This balanced approach seeks risk-first growth. Target monthly return is around 2.5%. It trims leverage and concentration while adding a defensive hedge, aiming for moderate drawdowns.

moves.note: Add inverse ETF for risk hedge

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, PLTU, MUU, SPAL) to 6% each.
Increase exposure to high-beta tech (MSFU) to 6%.
Buy SOXS as a hedge against tech weakness.
Maintain significant exposure to broad index ETFs (SPY, QQQ).
This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage and concentration.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretched growth with a ~4% monthly return. It leans heavily into leverage and concentration, accepting higher potential drawdowns and the risks of leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged and high-beta tech ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, MUU, SPAL) to zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to focus on income generation.
Maintain broad index ETFs (SPY, QQQ) for stability.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions over growth.
Expect lower volatility and reliable, though variable, income.
NAV can still decline in market downturns.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets ~1% monthly distributions. It cuts leverage and high-beta names, prioritizing income ETFs like QQQI. While aiming for low drawdown, NAV can still fall in selloffs.
